title: Treatment of alopecia areata (patchy hair loss)
what: This is when hair falls out in round patches. The doctor chooses a treatment to help the hair grow back.
why: When round bald patches appear on the scalp, in the beard, or in the eyebrows.
duration: a visit usually takes 20 to 30 minutes; hair usually grows back over several months
tell_doctor: When the patches appeared and whether they are growing
Thyroid disease and other long-term illnesses
Whether you had severe stress or an illness recently
Whether relatives have had the same

prepare.title: Hair
prepare.text: Do not cover the patches with powder or dye before the visit.

prepare.title: Photos
prepare.text: If you have photos showing how the patches changed, bring them.

bring: Results of past tests, if you have them
steps: The doctor asks when and how the hair loss began
Examines your scalp, sometimes with a special magnifier
Explains the treatment: skin products, sometimes injections into the patches
feel: If injections are given into the skin, a short stinging feeling
after: Use the products as your doctor prescribed
Hair does not grow back right away, so be patient
Sometimes thin light hairs grow first, then normal ones
Come for your check-up on the set date
red_flags: Hair falls out quickly all over your head
The skin patches become red, painful, or flaky

faq.a: No. Alopecia areata does not spread to other people.
Often yes, but the timing varies. Your doctor will tell you what to expect in your case.

reminders.text: Hair loss appointment tomorrow. Do not cover the patches, and bring any tests and photos you have.
